title: حِكَايَةُ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ
part: Night 101 · King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 529–532 (Night 101, continuing directly from nights-100), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 101 continues the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān. While the brothers ride back toward Constantinople, the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī, still disguised as a holy man, reaches the Muslim camp before them and tells the chamberlain that Bahrām and Rustam are in danger; he sends Bahrām’s brother Turkāsh with ten thousand horse, weakening the siege. Turkāsh meets the brothers safe and well, and they all marvel at the ascetic’s speed. Then the ascetic appears out of a pillar of dust crying that the infidels have fallen on the camp. Everyone kisses his hands except the vizier Dandān, who distrusts him; Sharrukān rebukes the vizier, the storyteller quotes a verse on false piety, and they reach the camp to find the Muslims on the point of rout. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الْحَادِيَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-ḥādiyatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the first after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and first night,
sentences.n: The night is numbered “the first after the hundred”, the hundred and first. al-ḥādiya is the ordinal “first” used in compound numbers; the print spells miʾa “hundred” with an alif, مائة, the old spelling, and the alif is not pronounced.

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُأَنَّ شَرْكَانَ هَنَّأَ أَخُوهُ ضَوْءَ الْمَكَانِ بِالسَّلَامَةِ وَشَكَرَهُ عَلَى أَفْعَالِهِ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna sharrukāna hannaʾa akhūhu ḍawʾa al-makāni bi-al-salāmati wa-shakarahu ʿalā afʿālihi
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that Sharrukān congratulated his-brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān on the safety, and thanked him for his deeds.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that Sharrukān congratulated his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān on his safe deliverance, and thanked him for all he had done.
sentences.n: The print runs السعيد and ان together (السعيدانّ); the spacing is kept. hannaʾa bi-, “congratulate on”: the verb chooses the bi-. The object “his brother” is printed in the nominative form akhūhu where Classical Arabic wants the accusative akhāhu — a Middle Arabic habit: akhū- is used for every case.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُمْ تَوَجَّهُوا مُجِدِّينَ الْمَسِيرَ طَالِبِينَ عَسَاكِرَهُمْ
sentences.tr: thumma innahum tawajjahū mujiddīna al-masīra ṭālibīna ʿasākirahum
sentences.l: Then they set-out, pressing-hard the march, seeking their armies.
sentences.i: Then they set off, pushing on in haste to rejoin their armies.
sentences.n: This picks up the last words of the night before. The shadda on توجّهوا is the print’s.

sentences.t: هَذَا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِهِمْ
sentences.tr: hādhā mā kāna min amrihim
sentences.l: This is what was of their affair.
sentences.i: So much for them.
sentences.n: The storyteller’s formula for leaving one thread and taking up another; the next sentence answers it with “and as for…”.

sentences.t: وَأَمَّا مَا كَانَ مِنْ أَمْرِ الْعَجُوزِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي فَإِنَّهَا لَمَّا لَاقَتْ عَسْكَرَ بَهْرَامَ وَرُسْتُمَ عَادَتْ إِلَى الْغَابَةِ وَأَخَذَتْ جَوَادَهَا وَرَكِبَتْهُ وَأَسْرَعَتْ فِى سَيْرِهَا حَتَّى أَشْرَفَتْ عَلَى عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ الْمُحَاصِرِينَ لِلْقُسْطَنْطِينِيَّةِ
sentences.tr: wa-ammā mā kāna min amri al-ʿajūzi dhāti al-dawāhī fa-innahā lammā lāqat ʿaskara bahrāma wa-rustama ʿādat ilā al-ghābati wa-akhadhat jawādahā wa-rakibathu wa-asraʿat fī sayrihā ḥattā ashrafat ʿalā ʿaskari al-muslimīna al-muḥāṣirīna li-al-qusṭanṭīniyyati
sentences.l: And as for what was of the affair of the old woman, She-of-the-Calamities: she, when she met the army of Bahrām and Rustam, returned to the thicket, and took her horse and rode it, and hastened in her going until she looked down on the army of the Muslims, the besiegers of Constantinople.
sentences.i: As for the old woman Dhāt al-Dawāhī: when she had met the army of Bahrām and Rustam, she went back to the thicket, took her horse, mounted and rode hard until she came in sight of the Muslim army besieging Constantinople.
sentences.n: ashrafa ʿalā, “come in sight of, look down upon”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. al-muḥāṣirīna li-, “besieging”: the li- marks the object of the participle.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهَا نَزَلَتْ وَأَخَذَتْ جَوَادَهَا وَأَتَتْ بِهِ إِلَى السُّرَادِقِ الَّذِي فِيهِ الْحَاجِبُ
sentences.tr: thumma innahā nazalat wa-akhadhat jawādahā wa-atat bihi ilā al-surādiqi alladhī fīhi al-ḥājibu
sentences.l: Then she dismounted, and took her horse and came with it to the pavilion which in-it was the chamberlain.
sentences.i: Then she dismounted and led her horse to the pavilion where the chamberlain was.
sentences.n: atā bi-, “bring”: the bi- marks what is brought — here she leads the horse.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأٰهَا نَهَضَ لَهَا قَائِمًا وَأَشَارَ إِلَيْهَا بِالْإِيمَاءِ وَقَالَ مَرْحَبًا بِالْعَابِدِ الزَّاهِدِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾāhā nahaḍa lahā qāʾiman wa-ashāra ilayhā bi-al-īmāʾi wa-qāla marḥaban bi-al-ʿābidi al-zāhidi
sentences.l: And when he saw her, he rose for her standing, and pointed to her with the gesture, and said: Welcome to the worshipper, the ascetic!
sentences.i: When he saw her he rose to his feet for her, greeted her with a gesture, and said, “Welcome to the devout ascetic!”
sentences.n: The print spells raʾāhā “he saw her” as رأها, without the long alif; the dagger alif supplies it. marḥaban bi-, “welcome to”: the bi- marks the one welcomed. He addresses her in the masculine — the chamberlain still takes the disguised old woman for a holy man.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَأَلَهَا عَمَّا جَرَى فَأَخْبَرَتْهُ بِخَبَرِهَا الْمُرْجِفِ وَبُهْتَانِهَا الْمُتْلِفِ
sentences.tr: thumma saʾalahā ʿammā jarā fa-akhbarathu bi-khabarihā al-murjifi wa-buhtānihā al-mutlifi
sentences.l: Then he asked her about what had happened, and she informed him of her alarming news and her ruinous slander.
sentences.i: Then he asked her what had happened, and she told him her alarming news and her ruinous lie.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-murjif / al-mutlif. akhbara bi-, “tell (someone) of”: the bi- marks the news told. murjif, “spreading alarm”; buhtān, “a lie that slanders”.

sentences.t: وَقَالَتْ إِنِّي أَخَافُ عَلَى الْأَمِيرِ رُسْتُمَ وَالْأَمِيرِ بَهْرَامَ لِأَنِّي قَدْ لَاقَيْتُهُمَا مَعَ عَسْكَرِهِمَا فِي الطَّرِيقِ وَأَرْسَلْتُهُمَا إِلَى الْمَلِكِ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ وَكَانَا فِي عِشْرِينَ أَلْفَ فَارِسٍ وَالْكُفَّارُ أَكْثَرُ مِنْهُمْ
sentences.tr: wa-qālat innī akhāfu ʿalā al-amīri rustama wa-al-amīri bahrāma li-annī qad lāqaytuhumā maʿa ʿaskarihimā fī al-ṭarīqi wa-arsaltuhumā ilā al-maliki wa-man maʿahu wa-kānā fī ʿishrīna alfa fārisin wa-al-kuffāru aktharu minhum
sentences.l: And she said: I fear for the emir Rustam and the emir Bahrām, because I met-them-both with their army on the road and sent them to the king and who is with him; and they-two were in twenty thousand horsemen, and the infidels are more than them.
sentences.i: She said, “I fear for the emirs Rustam and Bahrām. I met them on the road with their army and sent them on to the king and those with him; they had twenty thousand horsemen, but the infidels outnumber them.”
sentences.n: The print has اى, a misprint for الى (ilā, “to”), corrected here. khāfa ʿalā, “fear for”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَإِنِّي أَرَدْتُ فِي هَذِهِ السَّاعَةِ أَنْ تُرْسِلَ جُمْلَةً مِنْ عَسْكَرِكَ حَتَّى يَلْحَقُوهُمْ بِسُرْعَةٍ لِئَلَّا يَهْلِكُوا عَنْ آخِرِهِمْ وَقَالَتْ لَهُمُ الْعَجَلَ الْعَجَلَ
sentences.tr: wa-innī aradtu fī hādhihi al-sāʿati an tursila jumlatan min ʿaskarika ḥattā yalḥaqūhum bi-surʿatin li-allā yahlikū ʿan ākhirihim wa-qālat lahumu al-ʿajala al-ʿajala
sentences.l: And I wanted in this hour that you send a body of your army so that they overtake them with speed, lest they perish to their last. And she said to them: Haste! haste!
sentences.i: “I want you to send a body of your troops this very hour to reach them quickly, before they are destroyed to the last man.” And she urged them, “Hurry, hurry!”
sentences.n: ʿan ākhirihim, “to the last of them”: an idiom for “every one of them”. al-ʿajala al-ʿajala is accusative of urging, “(make) haste!”.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَاجِبُ وَالْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْهَا ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ انْحَلَّتْ عَزَائِمُهُمْ وَبَكَوْا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥājibu wa-al-muslimūna minhā dhālika al-kalāma inḥallat ʿazāʾimuhum wa-bakaw
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain and the Muslims heard from her that speech, their resolves came-undone, and they wept.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain and the Muslims heard this from her, their resolve gave way and they wept.

sentences.t: فَقَالَتْ لَهُمْ ذَاتُ الدَّوَاهِي اسْتَعِينُوا بِاللَّهِ وَاصْبِرُوا عَلَى هَذِهِ الرَّزِيَّةِ فَلَكُمْ أُسْوَةٌ بِمَنْ سَلَفَ مِنَ الْأُمَّةِ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةِ فَالْجَنَّةُ ذَاتُ الْقُصُورِ أَعَدَّهَا اللَّهُ لِمَنْ يَمُوتُ شَهِيدًا وَلَابُدَّ مِنَ الْمَوْتِ لِكُلِّ أَحَدٍ وَلَكِنَّهُ فِي الْجِهَادِ أَحْمَدُ
sentences.tr: fa-qālat lahum dhātu al-dawāhī istaʿīnū bi-allāhi wa-iṣbirū ʿalā hādhihi al-raziyyati fa-lakum uswatun bi-man salafa mina al-ummati al-muḥammadiyyati fa-al-jannatu dhātu al-quṣūri aʿaddahā allāhu li-man yamūtu shahīdan wa-lā budda mina al-mawti li-kulli aḥadin wa-lākinnahu fī al-jihādi aḥmadu
sentences.l: And She-of-the-Calamities said to them: Seek help in God, and be patient under this calamity, for you have an example in those who went before of the Muhammadan community; for the Garden, possessor of the palaces, God has prepared it for whoever dies a martyr; and there is no escape from death for every one, but it is in the holy war more-praiseworthy.
sentences.i: Dhāt al-Dawāhī said to them, “Seek God’s help and bear this calamity patiently: you have an example in those of Muhammad’s community who went before you. Paradise with its palaces God has made ready for whoever dies a martyr; everyone must die, but death in the holy war is the more praiseworthy.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: raziyya / muḥammadiyya; then jihād … aḥmad. istaʿāna bi-, “seek help from”: the bi- marks the helper; ṣabara ʿalā, “bear patiently”: the verb chooses the ʿalā; uswa bi-, “an example in”. The print sets و, لا and بد as one word, ولابد. The shaddas on الرزيّة, المحمديّة, فالجنّة, اعدّها and لكلّ are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْحَاجِبُ كَلَامَ اللَّعِينَةِ ذَاتِ الدَّوَاهِي دَعَا بِأَخِ الْأَمِيرِ بَهْرَامَ وَكَانَ فَارِسًا يُقَالُ لَهُ تُرْكَاشُ وَانْتَخَبَ لَهُ عَشَرَةَ آلَافِ فَارِسٍ أَبْطَالٍ عَوَابِسَ وَأَمَرَهُ بِالسَّيْرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-ḥājibu kalāma al-laʿīnati dhāti al-dawāhī daʿā bi-akhi al-amīri bahrāma wa-kāna fārisan yuqālu lahu turkāshu wa-intakhaba lahu ʿasharata ālāfi fārisin abṭālin ʿawābisa wa-amarahu bi-al-sayri
sentences.l: And when the chamberlain heard the speech of the accursed one, She-of-the-Calamities, he called for the brother of the emir Bahrām — and he was a horseman, it was said to him Turkāsh — and he chose for him ten thousand horsemen, heroes, grim-faced ones, and ordered him to the march.
sentences.i: When the chamberlain heard what the accursed Dhāt al-Dawāhī said, he sent for the emir Bahrām’s brother, a horseman named Turkāsh, picked out ten thousand grim-faced champions for him and ordered him to set out.
sentences.n: daʿā bi-, “send for, summon”: the bi- marks the one summoned. bi-akhi, “the brother of”: Classical Arabic wants bi-akhī in construct; the short form akh is the colloquial one. The name Turkāsh appears here for the first time and its vowels are our reading. amara bi-, “command”: the verb chooses the bi-.

sentences.t: فَسَارَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْيَوْمِ وَطُولَ اللَّيْلِ حَتَّى قَرُبَ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-sāra fī dhālika al-yawmi wa-ṭūla al-layli ḥattā qaruba mina al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And he marched in that day and the length of the night until he drew near to the Muslims.
sentences.i: He marched that day and all night long until he drew near the Muslims.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَصْبَحَ الصَّبَاحُ رَأَى شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارَ فَخَافَ عَلَى الْمُسْلِمِينَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aṣbaḥa al-ṣabāḥu raʾā sharrukānu dhālika al-ghubāra fa-khāfa ʿalā al-muslimīna
sentences.l: And when the morning became-morning, Sharrukān saw that dust, and feared for the Muslims.
sentences.i: When morning came, Sharrukān saw the dust rising, and feared for the Muslims.
sentences.n: “That dust” is the dust raised by Turkāsh’s riders; the storyteller has not mentioned it before.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ إِنَّ هَذِهِ عَسَاكِرُ مُقْبِلَةٌ عَلَيْنَا فَإِمَّا أَنْ يَكُونُوا مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَهَذَا هُوَ النَّصْرُ الْمُبِينُ وَإِمَّا أَنْ يَكُونُوا مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الْكُفَّارِ فَلَا اعْتِرَاضَ عَلَى الْأَقْدَارِ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla inna hādhihi ʿasākiru muqbilatun ʿalaynā fa-immā an yakūnū min ʿaskari al-muslimīna fa-hādhā huwa al-naṣru al-mubīnu wa-immā an yakūnū min ʿaskari al-kuffāri fa-lā iʿtirāḍa ʿalā al-aqdāri
sentences.l: And he said: These are armies advancing upon us; so either they are of the army of the Muslims, and this is the manifest victory; or they are of the army of the infidels, and there is no objecting to the decrees.
sentences.i: He said, “Those are armies coming toward us. Either they are a Muslim army, and that is plain victory; or they are an army of infidels, and there is no quarrelling with what is decreed.”
sentences.n: The print writes the “either … or” word as اما without hamza; it is read immā here. al-naṣr al-mubīn, “the manifest victory”, has a Qurʾānic ring (compare fatḥan mubīnan, 48:1).

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَتَى إِلَى أَخِيهِ ضَوْءِ الْمَكَانِ وَقَالَ لَهُ لَا تَخَفْ أَبَدًا فَإِنِّي أَفْدِيكَ بِرُوحِي مِنَ الرَّدَى
sentences.tr: thumma innahu atā ilā akhīhi ḍawʾi al-makāni wa-qāla lahu lā takhaf abadan fa-innī afdīka bi-rūḥī mina al-radā
sentences.l: Then he came to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him: Do not fear ever, for I ransom you with my soul from destruction.
sentences.i: Then he went to his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and said to him, “Have no fear at all: I will give my life to save you from death.”
sentences.n: fadā bi-, “ransom with”: the bi- marks the price paid, here “my soul”. The shadda on انّه is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَإِنْ كَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ مِنْ عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَهَذَا مِنْ مَزِيدِ الْإِنْعَامِ وَإِنْ كَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ أَعْدَاؤُنَا فَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ قِتَالِهِمْ لَكِنْ أَشْتَهِي أَنْ أُقَابِلَ الْعَابِدَ قَبْلَ مَوْتِي لِأَسْأَلَهُ أَنْ يَدْعُوَلِي أَنْ لَا أَمُوتَ إِلَّاشَهِيدًا
sentences.tr: fa-in kāna hāʾulāʾi min ʿaskari al-islāmi fa-hādhā min mazīdi al-inʿāmi wa-in kāna hāʾulāʾi aʿdāʾunā fa-lā budda min qitālihim lākin ashtahī an uqābila al-ʿābida qabla mawtī li-asʾalahu an yadʿuwa lī an lā amūta illā shahīdan
sentences.l: And if these are of the army of Islam, then this is of the increase of the bounty; and if these are our enemies, then there is no escape from fighting them. But I desire that I meet the worshipper before my death, to ask him that he pray for-me that I not die except a martyr.
sentences.i: “If they are an army of Islam, it is one more blessing; if they are our enemies, we have no choice but to fight them. Only I wish I could meet the holy man before I die, to ask him to pray that I may die only as a martyr.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-islām / al-inʿām. kāna hāʾulāʾi aʿdāʾunā: the nominative aʿdāʾunā is either Middle Arabic for Classical aʿdāʾanā, or hāʾulāʾi is a fronted predicate (“if our enemies are these”); the sense is the same. The print runs يدعو and لي together (يدعولي) and الا and شهيدا (الاشهيدا); the spacing is kept. daʿā li-, “pray for”: the li- marks the one prayed for. The shadda on بدّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَبَيْنَمَا هُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِالرَّايَاتِ قَدْ لَاحَتْ مَكْتُوبًا عَلَيْهَا لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ مُحَمَّدٌ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ
sentences.tr: fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-al-rāyāti qad lāḥat maktūban ʿalayhā lā ilāha illā allāhu muḥammadun rasūlu allāhi
sentences.l: And while they were thus, and behold, the banners had appeared, written on them: There is no god but God, Muhammad is the messenger of God.
sentences.i: While they were so, the banners came into view, and on them was written, “There is no god but God; Muhammad is the Messenger of God.”
sentences.n: wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: after idhā of surprise the bi- only marks what appears.

sentences.t: فَصَاحَ شَرْكَانُ كَيْفَ حَالُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ قَالُوا بِعَافِيَةٍ وَسَلَامَةٍ وَمَا أَتَيْنَا إِلَّاخَوْفًا عَلَيْكُمْ
sentences.tr: fa-ṣāḥa sharrukānu kayfa ḥālu al-muslimīna qālū bi-ʿāfiyatin wa-salāmatin wa-mā ataynā illā khawfan ʿalaykum
sentences.l: And Sharrukān shouted: How is the state of the Muslims? They said: In well-being and safety, and we did not come except fearing for you.
sentences.i: Sharrukān called out, “How are the Muslims?” They said, “Well and safe; we came only because we feared for you.”
sentences.n: The print runs الا and خوفا together (الاخوفا); the spacing is kept. khawfan ʿalā, “out of fear for”: the accusative gives the reason.

sentences.t: تَرَجَّلَ رَئِيسُ الْعَسْكَرِ عَنْ جَوَادِهِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ وَقَالَ يَا مَوْلَانَا كَيْفَ السُّلْطَانُ وَالْوَزِيرُ دَنْدَانُ وَرُسْتُمُ وَأَخِي بَهْرَامُ اَمَاهُمُ الْجَمِيعُ سَالِمُونَ
sentences.tr: tarajjala raʾīsu al-ʿaskari ʿan jawādihi wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi wa-qāla yā mawlānā kayfa al-sulṭānu wa-al-wazīru dandānu wa-rustamu wa-akhī bahrāmu a-mā humu al-jamīʿu sālimūna
sentences.l: The chief of the army dismounted from his horse and kissed the ground between his hands, and said: O our lord, how is the sultan, and the vizier Dandān, and Rustam, and my brother Bahrām? Are-not they all safe?
sentences.i: The commander of the troops dismounted, kissed the ground before him and said, “My lord, how is the sultan, and the vizier Dandān, and Rustam, and my brother Bahrām? Are they not all safe?”
sentences.n: The sentence has no “and” or “then” before tarajjala; the print runs straight on. “The sultan” is Ḍawʾ al-Makān. The vowels on اَمَا, a-mā “are … not?”, are the print’s; the question expects the answer yes.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ بِخَيْرٍ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla bi-khayrin
sentences.l: And he said: In good.
sentences.i: He said, “They are well.”

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَالَ لَهُ وَمَنِ الَّذِي أَخْبَرَكُمْ بِخَبَرِنَا قَالَ الزَّاهِدُ وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ أَنَّهُ لَقِيَ أَخِي بَهْرَامَ وَرُسْتُمَ وَأَرْسَلَهُمَا إِلَيْكُمْ وَقَالَ لَنَا إِنَّ الْكُفَّارَ قَدْ أَحَاطُوا بِهِمْ وَهُمْ كَثِيرُونَ
sentences.tr: thumma qāla lahu wa-mani alladhī akhbarakum bi-khabarinā qāla al-zāhidu wa-qad dhakara annahu laqiya akhī bahrāma wa-rustama wa-arsalahumā ilaykum wa-qāla lanā inna al-kuffāra qad aḥāṭū bihim wa-hum kathīrūna
sentences.l: Then he said to him: And who is the one who told you of our news? He said: The ascetic; and he mentioned that he met my brother Bahrām and Rustam and sent them to you, and said to us that the infidels had surrounded them, and they are many.
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān asked him, “And who told you about us?” He said, “The ascetic. He told us he had met my brother Bahrām and Rustam and sent them on to you, and he said the infidels had surrounded them in great numbers.”
sentences.n: aḥāṭa bi-, “surround”: the verb chooses the bi-. The shadda on انّه is the print’s. The disguised old woman is still “he” in the soldiers’ mouths.

sentences.t: وَمَا أَرَى الْأَمْرَ إِلَّا بِخِلَافِ ذَلِكَ وَأَنْتُمْ مَنْصُورُونَ
sentences.tr: wa-mā arā al-amra illā bi-khilāfi dhālika wa-antum manṣūrūna
sentences.l: And I do not see the matter except contrary to that, and you are made-victorious.
sentences.i: “But I see that things are quite otherwise, and you have won the day.”
sentences.n: The shadda on الّا is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالُوا لَهُ وَكَيْفَ وُصُولُ الزَّاهِدِ إِلَيْكُمْ فَقَالُوا لَهُ كَانَ سَائِرًا عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَقَطَعَ فِي يَوْمٍ وَلَيْلَةٍ مَسِيرَةَ عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ لِلْفَارِسِ الْمُجِدِّ
sentences.tr: fa-qālū lahu wa-kayfa wuṣūlu al-zāhidi ilaykum fa-qālū lahu kāna sāʾiran ʿalā qadamayhi wa-qaṭaʿa fī yawmin wa-laylatin masīrata ʿasharati ayyāmin li-al-fārisi al-mujiddi
sentences.l: And they said to him: And how was the arrival of the ascetic to you? And they said to him: He was going on his two feet, and he crossed in a day and a night the journey of ten days for the hard-pressing horseman.
sentences.i: They asked him, “And how did the ascetic reach you?” They answered, “He came on foot, and in a day and a night he covered what would take a horseman riding hard ten days.”
sentences.n: Both the question and its answer are introduced with “they said to him”: first Sharrukān’s party ask, then the newcomers answer. masīrat, “a journey of”: the distance one travels. The shadda on المجدّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ شَرْكَانُ لَا شَكَّ أَنَّهُ وَلِيُّ اللَّهِ وَأَيْنَ هُوَ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla sharrukānu lā shakka annahu waliyyu allāhi wa-ayna huwa
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said: No doubt that he is a friend of God. And where is he?
sentences.i: Sharrukān said, “Without doubt he is a saint of God. Where is he?”
sentences.n: waliyy allāh, “friend of God”, is the word for a saint, a holy man who works wonders. The shadda on وليّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: قَالُوا لَهُ تَرَكْنَاهُ عِنْدَ عَسْكَرِنَا أَهْلِ الْإِيمَانِ يُحَرِّضُهُمْ عَلَى قِتَالِ أَهْلِ الْكُفْرِ وَالطُّغْيَانِ
sentences.tr: qālū lahu taraknāhu ʿinda ʿaskarinā ahli al-īmāni yuḥarriḍuhum ʿalā qitāli ahli al-kufri wa-al-ṭughyāni
sentences.l: They said to him: We left him with our army, the people of faith, urging them on to the fighting of the people of unbelief and tyranny.
sentences.i: They said, “We left him with our army, the people of faith, spurring them on to fight the people of unbelief and tyranny.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-īmān / al-ṭughyān. ḥarraḍa ʿalā, “urge on to”: the verb chooses the ʿalā. The shadda on يحرّضهم is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ شَرْكَانُ بِذَلِكَ وَحَمِدُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى سَلَامَتِهِمْ وَسَلَامَةِ الزَّاهِدِ وَتَرَحَّمُوا عَلَى مَنْ قُتِلَ مِنْهُمْ وَقَالُوا كَانَ ذَلِكَ فِى الْكِتَابِ مَسْطُورًا
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa sharrukānu bi-dhālika wa-ḥamidū allāha ʿalā salāmatihim wa-salāmati al-zāhidi wa-taraḥḥamū ʿalā man qutila minhum wa-qālū kāna dhālika fī al-kitābi masṭūran
sentences.l: And Sharrukān rejoiced at that, and they praised God for their safety and the safety of the ascetic, and asked mercy upon whoever was killed of them, and said: That was in the Book written-down.
sentences.i: Sharrukān rejoiced at this. They praised God that they and the ascetic were safe, asked God’s mercy for those of them who had been killed, and said, “That was written in the Book.”
sentences.n: fariḥa bi-, “rejoice at”: the verb chooses the bi-. taraḥḥama ʿalā, “pray for God’s mercy on”. kāna dhālika fī al-kitābi masṭūran is a Qurʾānic phrase (17:58, 33:6): what happened was written beforehand. The damma on قُتل is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ سَارُوا مُجِدِّينَ فِي سَيْرِهِمْ فَبَيْنَمَاهُمْ كَذَلِكَ وَإِذَا بِغُبَارٍ قَدْ طَارَ حَتَّى سَدَّ الْأَقْطَارَ وَأَظْلَمَ مِنْهُ النَّهَارُ
sentences.tr: thumma sārū mujiddīna fī sayrihim fa-baynamā hum ka-dhālika wa-idhā bi-ghubārin qad ṭāra ḥattā sadda al-aqṭāra wa-aẓlama minhu al-nahāru
sentences.l: Then they went on, pressing-hard in their going; and while they were thus, and behold, a dust had flown up until it blocked the horizons, and the day grew-dark from it.
sentences.i: Then they rode on in haste. And while they were riding, a cloud of dust rose up until it blotted out the horizons and darkened the day.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-aqṭār / al-nahār. The print runs بينما and هم together (فبينماهم); the spacing is kept. wa-idhā bi-, “and behold”: the bi- only marks what appears. The shaddas on مجدّين and سدّ are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَنَظَرَ إِلَيْهِ شَرْكَانُ وَقَالَ إِنِّي أَخَافُ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْكُفَّارُ قَدْ كَسَرُوا عَسْكَرَ الْإِسْلَامِ لِأَنَّ هَذَا الْغُبَارَ سَدَّ الْمَشْرِقَيْنِ وَمَلَأَ الْخَافِقَيْنِ
sentences.tr: fa-naẓara ilayhi sharrukānu wa-qāla innī akhāfu an yakūna al-kuffāru qad kasarū ʿaskara al-islāmi li-anna hādhā al-ghubāra sadda al-mashriqayni wa-malaʾa al-khāfiqayni
sentences.l: And Sharrukān looked at it and said: I fear that the infidels have broken the army of Islam, because this dust has blocked the two east-points and filled the two horizons.
sentences.i: Sharrukān looked at it and said, “I fear the infidels have routed the army of Islam, for this dust has blotted out east and west and filled the world from end to end.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-mashriqayn / al-khāfiqayn, both duals. al-mashriqān, “the two easts”, means east and west together; al-khāfiqān, “the two horizons”, the whole world from east to west. kasara, “break”, is the usual word for routing an army. The shadda on سدّ is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ لَاحَ مِنْ تَحْتِ ذَلِكَ الْغُبَارِ عَمُودٌ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ أَشَدُّ سَوَادًا مِنْ حَالِكِ الْأَيَّامِ وَلَا زَالَتْ تَقْرُبُ مِنْهُمْ تِلْكَ الدِّعَامَةُ وَهِيَ أَشَدُّ مِنْ هَوْلِ يَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma lāḥa min taḥti dhālika al-ghubāri ʿamūdun mina al-ẓalāmi ashaddu sawādan min ḥāliki al-ayyāmi wa-lā zālat taqrubu minhum tilka al-diʿāmatu wa-hiya ashaddu min hawli yawmi al-qiyāmati
sentences.l: Then there appeared from under that dust a column of darkness, more intense in blackness than the pitch-black of the days; and that pillar did not cease drawing near to them, and it was more intense than the terror of the Day of Resurrection.
sentences.i: Then out from under the dust appeared a column of darkness, blacker than the blackest of days, and that pillar kept drawing nearer to them, more dreadful than the terror of the Day of Resurrection.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-ẓalām / al-ayyām, then diʿāma / qiyāma. ḥālik, “intensely black”; ḥālik al-ayyām, “the pitch-black of days”, is the darkest of days. The shaddas on اشدّ are the print’s.

sentences.t: فَتَسَارَعَتْ إِلَيْهَا الْخَيْلُ وَالرِّجَالُ لِيَنْظُرُوا مَا سَبَبُ سُوءِ هَذَا الْحَالِ فَرَأَوْهُ الزَّاهِدَ الْمُشَارَ إِلَيْهِ فَازْدَحَمُوا عَلَى تَقْبِيلِ يَدَيْهِ
sentences.tr: fa-tasāraʿat ilayhā al-khaylu wa-al-rijālu li-yanẓurū mā sababu sūʾi hādhā al-ḥāli fa-raʾawhu al-zāhida al-mushāra ilayhi fa-izdaḥamū ʿalā taqbīli yadayhi
sentences.l: And the horses and the men hastened to it, to see what was the cause of the evil of this state; and they saw him, the ascetic already-pointed-to, and they crowded on the kissing of his hands.
sentences.i: Horse and foot hurried toward it to see what lay behind this evil, and they found it was the ascetic already spoken of; and they crowded round to kiss his hands.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-rijāl / al-ḥāl. fa-raʾawhu al-zāhida, “they saw him, the ascetic”: the pronoun anticipates the noun it names, a common Middle Arabic construction. al-mushār ilayhi, “the one referred to”, is the stock phrase for someone already mentioned. izdaḥama ʿalā, “crowd round (to do)”: the verb chooses the ʿalā.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ يُنَادِي يَا أُمَّةَ خَيْرِ الْأَنَامِ وَمِصْبَاحِ الظَّلَامِ إِنَّ الْكُفَّارَ غَدَرُوا بِالْمُسْلِمِينَ فَأَدْرِكُوا عَسَاكِرَ الْمُوَحِّدِينَ وَأَنْقِذُوهُمْ مِنْ أَيْدِى الْكَفَرَةِ اللِّئَامِ فَإِنَّهُمْ هَجَمُوا عَلَيْهِمْ فِى الْخِيَامِ وَنَزَلَ بِهِمُ الْعَذَابُ الْمُهِينُ وَكَانُوا فِي مَكَانِهِمْ آمِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa yunādī yā ummata khayri al-anāmi wa-miṣbāḥi al-ẓalāmi inna al-kuffāra ghadarū bi-al-muslimīna fa-adrikū ʿasākira al-muwaḥḥidīna wa-anqidhūhum min aydī al-kafarati al-liʾāmi fa-innahum hajamū ʿalayhim fī al-khiyāmi wa-nazala bihimu al-ʿadhābu al-muhīnu wa-kānū fī makānihim āminīna
sentences.l: And he was calling: O community of the best of creatures and the lamp of the darkness! The infidels have acted-treacherously with the Muslims; so overtake the armies of the confessors-of-One-God and rescue them from the hands of the base infidels, for they fell upon them in the tents, and the humiliating punishment came down on them while they were in their place secure.
sentences.i: He was crying out, “O community of the best of mankind, the lamp in the darkness! The infidels have betrayed the Muslims. Go to the aid of the armies of God’s unity and rescue them from the hands of the vile infidels, for they fell upon them in their tents and humiliating torment came down on them while they sat in their camp thinking themselves safe.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-anām / al-ẓalām / al-liʾām / al-khiyām, then muhīn / āminīn. “The best of creatures” and “the lamp of darkness” are both the Prophet; the Muslims are his community. ghadara bi-, “betray”: the verb chooses the bi-. al-ʿadhāb al-muhīn, “the humiliating punishment”, is a Qurʾānic phrase. This time the report is true: having drawn ten thousand men away from the siege, she knows the camp has been attacked, as the end of the night shows.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ شَرْكَانُ ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ طَارَ قَلْبُهُ مِنْ شِدَّةِ الْخَفَقَانِ وَتَرَجَّلَ عَنْ جَوَادِةِ وَهُوَ حَيْرَانُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa sharrukānu dhālika al-kalāma ṭāra qalbuhu min shiddati al-khafaqāni wa-tarajjala ʿan jawādihi wa-huwa ḥayrānu
sentences.l: And when Sharrukān heard that speech, his heart flew from the violence of the throbbing, and he dismounted from his horse while he was bewildered.
sentences.i: When Sharrukān heard this, his heart leapt with violent throbbing, and he got down from his horse in bewilderment.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: khafaqān / ḥayrān. The print writes “his horse” جوادة, with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun -hu; read jawādihi. The shadda on وترجّل is the print’s.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ قَبَّلَ يَدَ الزَّاهِدِ وَرِجْلَيْهِ وَكَذَلِكَ أَخُوةُ ضَوْءُ الْمَكَانِ وَبَقِيَّةُ الْعَسْكَرِ مِنَ الرِّجَالِ وَالرُّكْبَانِ إِلَّا الْوَزِيرَ دَنْدَانَ فَإِنَّهُ لَمْ يَتَرَجَّلْ عَنْ جَوَادِةِ
sentences.tr: thumma qabbala yada al-zāhidi wa-rijlayhi wa-ka-dhālika akhūhu ḍawʾu al-makāni wa-baqiyyatu al-ʿaskari mina al-rijāli wa-al-rukbāni illā al-wazīra dandāna fa-innahu lam yatarajjal ʿan jawādihi
sentences.l: Then he kissed the hand of the ascetic and his two feet; and likewise his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān, and the rest of the army, of the men-on-foot and the riders — except the vizier Dandān, for he did not dismount from his horse.
sentences.i: Then he kissed the ascetic’s hand and feet, and so did his brother Ḍawʾ al-Makān and the rest of the army, foot and horse alike — all except the vizier Dandān, who did not get down from his horse.
sentences.n: The print writes the pronoun -hu with tāʾ marbūṭa twice here, اخوة “his brother” and جوادة “his horse”; read akhūhu and jawādihi. The shaddas on قبّل and يترجّل are the print’s.

sentences.t: وَقَالَ وَاللَّهِ إِنَّ قَلْبِي نَافِرٌ مِنْ هَذَا الزَّاهِدِ لِأَنِّي مَا عَرَفْتُ لِلْمُتَنَطِّعِينَ فِى الدِّينِ غَيْرَ الْمَفَاسِدِ فَاتْرُكُوةُ وَأَدْرِكُوا أَصْحَابَكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ فَإِنَّ هَذَا مِنَ الْمَطْرُودِينَ عَنْ بَابِ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-qāla wa-allāhi inna qalbī nāfirun min hādhā al-zāhidi li-annī mā ʿaraftu li-al-mutanaṭṭiʿīna fī al-dīni ghayra al-mafāsidi fa-utrukūhu wa-adrikū aṣḥābakumu al-muslimīna fa-inna hādhā mina al-maṭrūdīna ʿan bābi raḥmati rabbi al-ʿālamīna
sentences.l: And he said: By God, my heart shies from this ascetic, because I have not known in the over-zealous in religion other than the corruptions. So leave him, and overtake your companions the Muslims; for this one is of those driven away from the door of the mercy of the Lord of the worlds.
sentences.i: He said, “By God, my heart turns from this ascetic. I have never known anything but mischief from those who make a show of zeal in religion. Leave him and go to the help of your comrades, the Muslims: this man is one of those driven from the door of the mercy of the Lord of the worlds.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-zāhid / al-mafāsid. mutanaṭṭiʿ, “one who overdoes things, a zealot”: the li- marks those in whom he has found mischief (“I have known of them”). The print writes “leave him” فاتركوة, with tāʾ marbūṭa for the pronoun -hu; read fa-utrukūhu. The shadda on للمتنطّعين is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَكَمْ غَزَوْتُ مَعَ الْمَلِكِ عُمَرَ بْنِ النُّعْمَانِ وَدُسْتُ أَرَاضِيَ هَذَا الْمَكَانِ
sentences.tr: fa-kam ghazawtu maʿa al-maliki ʿumara bni al-nuʿmāni wa-dustu arāḍiya hādhā al-makāni
sentences.l: For how-many-times I raided with King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and trod the lands of this place!
sentences.i: “How many campaigns I fought with King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, and how often I trod the lands of this country!”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-nuʿmān / al-makān. Dandān means he knows the country and the enemy’s ways.

sentences.t: فَقَالَ لَهُ شَرْكَانُ دَعْ هَذَا الظَّنَّ الْفَاسِدَ أَمَانَظَرْتَ إِلَى هَذَا الْعَابِدِ وَهُوَ يُحَرِّضُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ عَلَى الْقِتَالِ وَلَا يُبَالِي بِالسُّيُوفِ وَالنِّبَالِ
sentences.tr: fa-qāla lahu sharrukānu daʿ hādhā al-ẓanna al-fāsida a-mā naẓarta ilā hādhā al-ʿābidi wa-huwa yuḥarriḍu al-muʾminīna ʿalā al-qitāli wa-lā yubālī bi-al-suyūfi wa-al-nibāli
sentences.l: And Sharrukān said to him: Leave this corrupt suspicion. Have you not looked at this worshipper while he urges the believers to the fighting and does not care for the swords and the arrows?
sentences.i: Sharrukān said to him, “Put away this wicked suspicion. Have you not seen this holy man spurring on the believers to battle, with no care for swords and arrows?”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-qitāl / al-nibāl. The print runs اما and نظرت together (امانظرت); the spacing is kept. bālā bi-, “care about”: the verb chooses the bi-. The print spells al-muʾminīn without the hamza, المومنين. The shadda on يحرّض is the print’s.

sentences.t: فَلَا تَغْتَبْهُ لِأَنَّ الْغِيبَةَ مَذْمُومَةٌ وَلُحُومَ الصَّالِحِينَ مَسْمُومَةٌ
sentences.tr: fa-lā taghtabhu li-anna al-ghībata madhmūmatun wa-luḥūma al-ṣāliḥīna masmūmatun
sentences.l: So do not backbite him, because backbiting is blameworthy, and the flesh of the righteous is poisoned.
sentences.i: “Do not speak ill of him behind his back: backbiting is a sin, and the flesh of holy men is poison.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: madhmūma / masmūma. To backbite is, in the Qurʾān (49:12), to eat a brother’s dead flesh; the proverb adds that the flesh of the righteous is poisoned — slander a saint and it will destroy you.

sentences.t: وَانْظُرْ إِلَى تَحْرِيضِهِ لَنَا عَلَى قِتَالِ أَعْدَائِنَا وَلَوْلَا أَنَّ اللَّهَ تَعَالَى يُحِبُّهُ مَا طَوَى لَهُ الْبَعِيدَ مِنَ الْأَرْضِ بَعْدَ أَنْ أَوْقَعَهُ سَابِقًا فِى الْعَذَابِ الشَّدِيدِ
sentences.tr: wa-unẓur ilā taḥrīḍihi lanā ʿalā qitāli aʿdāʾinā wa-lawlā anna allāha taʿālā yuḥibbuhu mā ṭawā lahu al-baʿīda mina al-arḍi baʿda an awqaʿahu sābiqan fī al-ʿadhābi al-shadīdi
sentences.l: And look at his urging of us to the fighting of our enemies. And were it not that God the Exalted loves him, He would not have folded up for him the far of the earth, after He had made him fall formerly into the severe torment.
sentences.i: “See how he urges us to fight our enemies. If God Most High did not love him, He would not have folded up the distances of the earth for him, after once letting him fall into cruel torment.”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-baʿīd / al-shadīd. ṭawā al-arḍ, “fold up the earth”, is the miracle of a saint who crosses great distances in a moment — it answers the soldiers’ report of a ten-day journey made in a day and a night. The “severe torment” is the captivity the ascetic claimed to have suffered at the hands of the Christians.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ شَرْكَانَ أَمَرَ أَنْ يُقَدِّمُوا بَغْلَةً نُوبِيَّةً إِلَى الزَّاهِدِ لِيَرْكَبَهَا وَقَالَ لَهُ ارْكَبْ أَيُّهَا الزَّاهِدُ النَّاسِكُ الْعَابِدُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna sharrukāna amara an yuqaddimū baghlatan nūbiyyatan ilā al-zāhidi li-yarkabahā wa-qāla lahu irkab ayyuhā al-zāhidu al-nāsiku al-ʿābidu
sentences.l: Then Sharrukān ordered that they bring forward a Nubian she-mule to the ascetic for him to ride it, and said to him: Ride, O ascetic, devotee, worshipper!
sentences.i: Then Sharrukān ordered a Nubian mule to be brought for the ascetic to ride, and said to him, “Mount, O pious and devout ascetic!”
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-zāhid / al-ʿābid. A mule, not a horse, is the proper mount for a holy man; Nubian mules were prized.

sentences.t: فَلَمْ يَقْبَلْ ذَلِكَ وَامْتَنَعَ مِنَ الرُّكُوبِ وَأَظْهَرَ الزُّهْدَ لِيَنٰلَ الْمَطْلُوبَ
sentences.tr: fa-lam yaqbal dhālika wa-imtanaʿa mina al-rukūbi wa-aẓhara al-zuhda li-yanāla al-maṭlūba
sentences.l: And he did not accept that, and refused the riding, and displayed the asceticism to obtain the sought-thing.
sentences.i: But the ascetic would not accept, refused to ride and made a show of self-denial, to get what he was after.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-rukūb / al-maṭlūb. The print spells li-yanāla “to obtain” لينل, without the long alif; the dagger alif supplies it.

sentences.t: وَمَا دَرَوْا أَنَّ هَذَا الزَّاهِدَ الْعَاهِرَ هُوَ الَّذِي قَالَ فِي مِثْلِهِ الشَّاعِرُ
sentences.tr: wa-mā daraw anna hādhā al-zāhida al-ʿāhira huwa alladhī qāla fī mithlihi al-shāʿiru
sentences.l: And they did not know that this ascetic, the whoremonger, is the one about whose like the poet said:
sentences.i: And they did not know that this lecherous ascetic was the very kind of whom the poet said:
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-ʿāhir / al-shāʿir. ʿāhir is a fornicator, a debauchee; the storyteller says it of the old woman herself, and keeps her masculine disguise.

sentences.t: صَلَّى وَصَامَ لِاَمْرٍ كَانَ يَطْلُبُهُ * لَمَّا قَضَى الْاَمْرَ لَا صَلَّى وَلَا صَامَا
sentences.tr: ṣallā wa-ṣāma li-amrin kāna yaṭlubuhu * lammā qaḍā al-amra lā ṣallā wa-lā ṣāmā
sentences.l: He prayed and fasted for a matter he was seeking; * when he had accomplished the matter, he neither prayed nor fasted.
sentences.i: He prayed and fasted for a thing he wanted; * once he had his way, he neither prayed nor fasted.
sentences.n: The vowels of the verse are the print’s; it writes hamza-less alif with a fatḥa in لِاَمْرٍ and الْاَمْرَ.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ ذَلِكَ الزَّاهِدَ مَازَالَ مَاشِيًا بَيْنَ الْخَيْلِ وَالرِّجَالِ كَأَنَّهُ الثَّعْلَبُ الْمُحْتَالُ لِلِاغْتِيَالِ وَصَارَ رَافِعًا صَوْتَهُ بِتِلَاوَةِ الْقُرْآنِ وَتَسْبِيحِ الرَّحْمَنِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna dhālika al-zāhida mā zāla māshiyan bayna al-khayli wa-al-rijāli ka-annahu al-thaʿlabu al-muḥtālu li-al-ightiyāli wa-ṣāra rāfiʿan ṣawtahu bi-tilāwati al-qurʾāni wa-tasbīḥi al-raḥmāni
sentences.l: Then that ascetic did not cease walking between the horses and the men, as though he were the fox, the trickster, for the ambush; and he began raising his voice with the recitation of the Qurʾān and the glorifying of the Merciful.
sentences.i: And all the while that ascetic went on foot among the horsemen and footmen, like a cunning fox lying in wait, raising his voice in reciting the Qurʾān and glorifying the Merciful.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-rijāl / al-muḥtāl / al-ightiyāl, then al-qurʾān / al-raḥmān. The print sets ما and زال as one word, مازال. ightiyāl, “taking unawares, assassination”.

sentences.t: وَمَازَالُوا سَائِرِينَ حَتَّى أَشْرَفُوا عَلَى عَسْكَرِ الْإِسْلَامِ فَوَجَدَهُمْ شَرْكَانُ فِي حَالَةِ الِانْكِسَارِ وَالْحَاجِبُ قَدْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَى الْهَزِيمَةِ وَالْفِرَارِ وَسَيْفُ الرُّومِ يَعْمَلُ بَيْنَ الْأَبْرَارِ وَالْفُجَّارِ
sentences.tr: wa-mā zālū sāʾirīna ḥattā ashrafū ʿalā ʿaskari al-islāmi fa-wajadahum sharrukānu fī ḥālati al-inkisāri wa-al-ḥājibu qad ashrafa ʿalā al-hazīmati wa-al-firāri wa-sayfu al-rūmi yaʿmalu bayna al-abrāri wa-al-fujjāri
sentences.l: And they did not cease going until they looked down on the army of Islam, and Sharrukān found them in a state of the breaking, and the chamberlain had come to the edge of the rout and the flight, and the sword of the Rūm was working among the righteous and the wicked.
sentences.i: They rode on until they came in sight of the army of Islam, and Sharrukān found it broken: the chamberlain on the point of defeat and flight, and the sword of the Byzantines at work among good men and bad alike.
sentences.n: Rhymed prose: al-inkisār / al-firār / al-fujjār. ashrafa ʿalā is used twice: “come in sight of” and then “be on the brink of”. al-Rūm are the Byzantine Greeks.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
